item.title: Brady Hart gets start as Texas A&M makes change at quarterback for Oklahoma game
item.description: Brady Hart got his first start for Texas A&M on Saturday at Oklahoma, replacing an ineffective Marcel Reed in the Aggies' next-to-last game of the regular season. (Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) NORMAN, Okla. - Mike Elko has opted for a change in quarterback for Texas A& M 's final road game of a disappointing 2026 season. Brady Hart's first career start Saturday against Oklahoma comes one week after he received his most meaningful playing time of the season. The sophomore quarterback entered the Aggies' 22-7 loss to Tennessee last week with under 3 minutes remaining and completed two of his three pass attempts for 22 yards before throwing an interception. Following the consistent struggles of returning starter Marcel Reed, Hart's entry received a standing ovation by fans at Kyle Field. A week later, Hart was handed the offense from the opening snap against an Oklahoma (6-4) defense which ranks fifth in the SEC in yards allowed (294.6). Hart had appeared in four games this season for the Aggies (4-6), completing 14 of 24 passes for 165 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions. His most productive outing came in A&M's blowout win over The Citadel , when Hart completed 8 of 12 passes for 107 yards and a touchdown. He also had two carries for 8 yards. Saturday's change came after an increasingly rough stretch for an Aggie offense that entered the OU matchup ranked 13th in the SEC in total offense (341.2). A&M managed just 179 yards against Tennessee, never reached the red zone and scored seven points. Reed completed nine of 22 passes for 71 yards and an interception before Hart was put in the game. Elko took responsibility for the offense after the loss, calling it "inept" and "completely non-functional" while pushing back against the idea that the problems could be attributed solely to Reed. The opportunity in Norman put Hart in the middle of the Aggies' final push for bowl eligibility, needing to win their final two games in order to receive an invitation. item.title: Wilton field hockey scores with 52 seconds left to beat Branford for first CIAC title since 2015
item.description: Casey O'Connor, center, of Wilton and her teammates celebrate their 1-0 victory against Branford in the CIAC Class M Field Hockey Championship in Wethersfield on November 10, 2026. O'Connor scored the winning goal. (Arnold Gold/Hearst Connecticut Media) WETHERSFIELD - Wilton field hockey player Maeve Ryder had barely gotten her cleat back on when the ball found her stick. She immediately sent in a hard cross, and Casey O'Connor was waiting to tip it over the goalie's head with 52 seconds left to play, giving No. 2 Wilton its first CIAC title in over a decade with a 1-0 win over No. 1 Branford on Saturday in the Class M final at Wethersfield High School. It is Wilton's seventh CIAC title but its first since 2015. O'Connor had just been released from a penalty and got herself in position to flick in the game-winning goal, while Ryder lost her shoe in a collision and had just pounded her foot back into it when she got the ball. "I came right off the penalty box and I knew we had less than a minute left and I knew we had to do this and end it because I was too tired to play 7 vs. 7," O'Connor said. "I stuck my stick out in front and I saw it going up. When it went in, I was ecstatic. It was so much fun." Wilton coach Leon Kerr said the play developed just as they practiced it, other than Ryder's shoe coming off. "We have been working on that with a packed circle and trying to put two forwards in there and getting the ball across and get a stick on it," Kerr said. "Once you get a stick on a hard pass, it will pop and we know that this goalie likes to go flat, so we worked on trying to pop the ball over her." O'Connor is one of 12 seniors on the Wilton team, making this run to a championship even more special. "This means the world," O'Connor said. "We have worked for this, and the coaches have done such a great job preparing us. It was a collective effort and everyone did their part." Wilton controlled much of the game, though Ellie Meyran of Branford broke out for several scoring chances without converting. Branford was playing in its third straight Class M title game and was the defending champion. "We have been resilient all season and it was unfortunate that goal came so late because it didn't give us a chance to respond," Branford coach Peter Frye said. "We knew this was going to be a really tight game and expected a one-goal game." Branford was playing in its 18th championship game, while Wilton was making its 12th trip to a final. item.title: Maple Leafs Take Sudden Drastic Step After 8th-Straight Loss
item.description: Jim Hiller Maple Leafs Getty Maple Leafs Jim Hiller Getty The Toronto Maple Leafs are in the midst of an eight-game losing skid after having dropped a 4-3 shootout decision against the struggling Los Angeles Kings on Thursday night. While they were finally able to break their pointless skid, they’ve still not won a single game in the month of November. Additionally, their six straight losses on home ice set a mark that hadn’t been seen in multiple decades. In a drastic step, the Maple Leafs have now brought in a renowned sports psychologist to try and turn the tide. Toronto Maple Leafs Bring In Renowned Sports Psychologist To Speak To The Organization Getty Maple Leafs Jim Hiller On Friday morning, the Maple Leafs were not only visited by Rory McIlroy, but also by sports psychologist Dr. Bob Rotella. McIlroy read the starting lineup in the dressing room prior to the game on Thursday night, and later visited again with the team the following day, along with Dr. Rotella, the author of multiple books, including the New York Times best seller “How Champions Think” in 2015. “If I can win the Masters, then the Leafs can win the Stanley Cup,” McIlroy said. “What an honour for us to have him,” Hiller said of the six-time major champion. “We got a chance to meet with him a little bit as coaches and then the players. If you are wondering what an athlete, a pro, a winner and all the things, you can add all the superlatives you want, that’s him. “He’s gone through some difficult times at certain times too and he just powered through so I think he’s just a great example for us right here right now.” Jim Hiller Addresses Job Security Hiller also addressed his job security amidst rumors that he could potentially be let go not even halfway into his first year with the club. “Not something I think about too much. I appreciate that John did that. My job is to win games. We haven’t won enough, so I’ll get them ready to win tomorrow (on Saturday against the Columbus Blue Jackets),” Hiller said. “Yeah, I mean, listen, we want to win. I told you that. I love hockey. I love winning. And when those two things collide, when you don’t win, it doesn’t feel very good. I’ve said that multiple times,” Hiller said. item.description: COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 7: Head Coach Ryan Day of the Ohio State Buckeyes talks with the referees during a timeout in the second quarter of the game against the Oregon Ducks at Ohio Stadium on November 7, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) Getty Ohio State head coach Ryan Day is taking some heat for a bizarre penalty against Nebraska. Day was flagged for an unusual penalty, one that took place on a big early play for the Buckeyes. The Ohio State coach was already facing scrutiny for his team’s unusual struggles this season, and took more heat for the penalty. As USA Today’s John Leuzzi noted, Day was flagged for sideline interference during a 67-yard touchdown pass from Luke Fahey to Jeremiah Smith. “The touchdown briefly appeared to be in jeopardy when a flag was thrown after the snap, but the penalty, a sideline interference call against Ryan Day, did not negate the explosive scoring drive — likely much to the happiness of Day and Smith, who is trying to win the Heisman Trophy,” Leuzzi wrote. The Match Lyon’s new head coach Carlos Vicens would be given a proper welcome to Ligue 1 with a trip to the Stade Pierre-Mauroy to face Carlo Ancelotti’s Lille. Coming out of the international break, Lille were in the runners-up spot and wanted to maintain the two-point gap with Paris Saint-Germain. It was a cagey start to the game, with neither side having much luck finding space within the box. Shots were largely restrained to tame efforts from outside the box. Nabil Bentaleb’s swipe wide for the hosts was almost bettered by Corentin Tolisso’s effort that forced Berke Özer into a stretching save. It took forty minutes for the game to come to life, with Mads Bidstrup firing home off the post from a messy moment of defending by Alexsandro. The centre-back, who so often looks composed at the back, got his first touch wrong in an interception in the box, allowing Corentin Tolisso to poke the ball to Bidstrup. Shortly after the restart, Lyon had the ball in the back of the net again when Abner Vinícius found Ernest Nuamah in the box. The Ghanaian international had a tidy finish that would ultimately be ruled out following a pitch-side review by the referee, after Bidstrup was spotted colliding with the goalkeeper and impeding his ability to save the shot. Ancelotti brought on Japanese international Ayase Ueda at half-time as he looked to give a shot in the arm to his flagging side. The striker was lively from the moment he was introduced, firing from distance to provide Dominik Greif a warning shot that things might not be so comfortable in the second half for the Lyon goalkeeper. Despite the renewed energy, Lille were struggling to get chances within the box. They were mostly restricted to efforts from distance, as Ngal’ayel Mukau, Bentaleb, and Nathan Ngoy each took turns trying to fire Les Dogues level. Olivier Giroud was thrown on as Lille searched for an equaliser, but it was not enough for a side that, despite their success in the league thus far, has struggled to consistently find the back of the net. There was desperation and chaos in the Lyon box in the final minutes, but it was not enough to force a last-gasp twist as Lyon held onto their narrow win and delivered Lille their first home defeat in the league this season. item.title: 49ers waive ex-Bills, Saints WR with 9,869 career receiving yards
item.description: 49ers waive ex-Bills, Saints WR with 9,869 career receiving yards originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Francisco 49ers have needed wide receiver help this season, as they've dealt with a ridiculous string of injuries. But heading into Week 11, it appears they're getting healthy. Demarcus Robinson and Deebo Samuel have been back, and now Mike Evans appears set to play in Sunday Night Football against the Minnesota Vikings . The return of these WRs, along with the trade for Keenan Allen, has really shaken up this WR room. One fallout of this WR room improving and getting healthier is a veteran wide receiver who's spent time with the Buffalo Bills and New Orleans Saints , Brandin Cooks, who the 49ers announced on Saturday was being waived prior to Week 11. 49ers waive WR Brandin Cooks prior to Week 11 "The following player has been waived: WR Brandin Cooks," the 49ers announced. "In addition, CB Nate Hobbs game status has been downgraded from questionable to out." San Francisco's WR room is getting healthier, and that's led the team to move on from Cooks this season. Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Demarcus Robinson, Keenan Allen, Jordan Watkins, and Jacob Cowing are all healthy for the 49ers right now. While this is an older WR room that does need depth, the 49ers do not need a seventh WR in Cooks, especially with De'Zhuan Stribling potentially coming back later this season as well. Cooks played in five games for the 49ers this season, catching five of his 10 targets for 58 yards and a touchdown. The 49ers are Cooks' seventh NFL franchise, and the most recent one after spending 2025 with the Saints and Bills. MORE : Grading NFL trade deadline debuts, from Kirk Cousins' Vikings return to Josh Downs' impressive day He has 9,869 receiving yards in his NFL career, only 131 yards away from reaching 10,000 for his career, which would be quite an accomplishment. Cooks also has 61 receiving touchdowns and 739 receptions on 1,145 targets in 178 games played in his 13-year NFL career that began with the Saints back in 2014 after being taken in Round 1 at No. 20 overall in the 2014 NFL Draft. If this is it for Cooks, he's had an incredible career. But with plenty of WR-needy teams around the NFL, Cooks, at 33 years old, could realistically sign somewhere this season and chase 10,000 receiving yards. A return to the Los Angeles Rams would make sense. But with the 49ers getting healthier in the wide receiver room, they've decided to move on from Cooks. He'll hit waivers, where he could be claimed by a team. If he clears, he'll be a free agent and could choose any team, including the 49ers, to sign with. item.title: Browns Todd Monken Gets Major NFL Prediction
item.description: Head coach Todd Monken of the Cleveland Browns Getty A 6-4 record is not, generally, cause for celebration in the NFL, but if you’re the coach of the Cleveland Browns and coming off two years in which the team scored eight total wins, it’s a lot more noteworthy. That’s where Browns coach Todd Monken is now, and all things considered, he has done a pretty good job. He has gotten something out of what had been the husk of Deshaun Watson’s career, he has managed to run an offense with an entirely new offensive line that includes two rookies, he has maximized two rookies and a second-year player as his top pass-catchers, he has kept the defense’s standard high despite trading away Myles Garrett and while teams like Dallas and Philadelphia have undergone much hand-wringing over having one first-year coordinator on staff, all three of Monken’s coordinators are first-timers, and doing just fine. All that makes the 6-4 that much more impressive. And Monken could be rewarded for that. Browns’ Todd Monken vs. 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan As of now, in fact, Monken is the favorite to win the NFL’s Coach of the Year Award here in 2026. Browns fans might roll their eyes at that–Kevin Stefanski won it with the Browns, twice, and his name does not evoke much fondness in Northeast Ohio. But it is an indication of how Monken is being viewed around the NFL. Monken opened the year as a plus-1,800 proposition for the award, tied for 10th among all coaches. He is now neck-and-neck with 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan for COY, with Monken at 31% to win on the Kalshi prediction market, and Shanahan at 30%. item.title: Arsenal 'pained' by dropping points at Newcastle, says Arteta
item.description: Mikel Arteta's Arsenal were held 2-2 by Newcastle (ANDY BUCHANAN) Mikel Arteta said he could sense the anguish among his players despite opening up a six-point lead at the top of the Premier League with a 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday. The Gunners missed the chance to extend their winning league run to six games after conceding twice in a careless spell just after half-time. Eberechi Eze's strike was scant reward for Arsenal's dominance in the first half. Goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw then put Arteta's men at risk of just a second defeat this season until Noni Madueke rescued a point. Arsenal moved six points clear of Brighton, who can close the gap to three with victory at Hull on Sunday, and Manchester City ahead of their trip to the Emirates Stadium next weekend. "We've been here six or seven years with me and it's the best we've played here by far and we have won a few times," said Arteta. "Today the margins should have been much, much bigger and they weren't. That's the pain that we are all feeling. It's not just me, it's a pain that the players are feeling, but immediately I could sense that and that's the standard that we need." Even more damaging than the loss of two points could be a shoulder injury to goalkeeper David Raya. The Spanish international was forced off shortly after Newcastle's second goal and would be a major loss if he is sidelined for a lengthy period. "Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is never good news," added Arteta. "He will get assessed now and he will probably have an MRI tomorrow to see what it is exactly because at the moment, I don't know." kca/nf

item.title: U17 World Cup: Patetuci hails opening win and squad strength
item.description: U17 World Cup: Patetuci hails opening win and squad strength Coach pleased with the team's approach Credits: Nelson Terme /CBF Brazil's men's U-17 national team opened their World Cup campaign with a 2-1 win over Ireland on Saturday (21) in Doha, Qatar. After the match, coach Carlos Eduardo Patetuci discussed the challenges posed by the Europeans' defensive organization, his team's improvement in the second half and the importance of the result for the rest of the tournament. “It's an opening match against a European team that plays a very organized game. They set up with a back five at times, switching to a 4-4-2. The emotional factor also made it a very back-and-forth game. With those nerves, we lost the second balls and couldn't sustain control of the game. We would take control and then lose it,” he explained. Patetuci did, however, see a significant improvement in his team during the second half. According to him, Brazil were able to execute the movements laid out in their game plan more consistently and find greater stability in the match. “For an opening match, the most important thing was that in the second half, especially after the substitutions, we improved a lot and were more consistent in our movements and in implementing our style of play. We got the opening win, which was our main objective, to give us peace of mind and confidence for the rest of the competition,” he said. Their next match is against Tanzania on Monday (23). Patetuci is treating the encounter as another final and highlighted the attacking qualities of their opponents, who have skillful players capable of dribbling and improvisation. The coach also pointed to spells of disorganization in the African side as something Brazil intend to exploit. “They're a very strong attacking team, with plenty of dribbling and improvisation too. But at the same time, they struggle to stay organized for long stretches; they lose their shape and become disorganized frequently. We'll take advantage of that with our style of play, looking to be more emotionally composed from the start, implement our game plan, control the game and beat Tanzania too,” he said. Beyond the result, the coach praised the team's competitive spirit and the contribution of the players who came on during the match. For Patetuci, the substitutes' performances underline the importance of being able to count on the entire squad throughout a short, demanding competition. “I was very pleased. Brazil competed hard and fought for every ball. It showed the importance of the collective effort: the players who came on did extremely well, performing at an excellent level. We competed and found our balance in the second half, and that makes us happy because we can count on everyone. Our squad is strong, and we keep moving forward,” he concluded. With three points secured in their opener, Brazil return to action on Monday (23) against Tanzania in the second round of Group I at the U-17 World Cup. The match kicks off at 6 p.m.

item.title: Patience isn't just a virtue for Spurs' Tarris Reed Jr. It's a necessity
item.description: San Antonio Spurs center Tarris Reed Jr. (10) plays in the second half of a preseason NBA game against the Phoenix Suns at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Wednesday, Oct. 14, 2026. The Spurs defeated the Suns 123-103. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) Spurs rookie Tarris Reed Jr. has learned the hard way the value of patience. As a freshman at Michigan in 2022-23, Reed spent most of every game glued to the end of the bench, only getting his chance to play once the score was out of hand and the outcome decided. "I freaking hated it," Reed said. Three years later, Reed finds himself in a familiar spot with the Spurs. The difference is that the 23-year-old sitting at the end of Mitch Johnson's bench has a much different perspective on what it means to be there. "My mindset has changed," Reed said. "I'm in the NBA now. I get to play these games. I get to be on the best team in the NBA and having fun doing it." Don't get it twisted. Reed still wants to play. It's just now he understands the reward that comes with waiting his turn. In June, the Spurs traded into the bottom of the first round of the draft to select Reed with the No. 26 overall pick. A 6-foot-10, 270-pound mountain of a center, Reed has displayed a nose for rebounding and a knack for wringing every ounce of sweat out of every second of court time he receives. So far, those seconds have been few and far between. Heading into Saturday's game against New Orleans at the Frost Bank Center, Reed had totaled 54 minutes over nine appearances, most of it in mop-up duty. Given the limited playing time, Reed's raw numbers have not jumped off the page. He is averaging 2.0 points and 2.9 rebounds. Look a little closer, however, and it is hard to miss the hint of what he might do with a bigger opportunity. Reed is averaging an astronomical 17.3 rebounds per 36 minutes. "I call him a walking 10 boards," forward Devin Vassell said. "As soon as he gets in the game, I feel like he's getting 10 boards." Reed's patience is being tested at a time when the Spurs are still searching for answers with their second unit. Entering Saturday, San Antonio was 39 points per 100 possessions worse when All-Star Victor Wembanyama went to the bench. Luke Kornet, the 31-year-old veteran charged with filling in for Wembanyama, has had his share of struggles. That leaves an obvious question: What does Reed have to do to earn a more prolonged look at the backup center role? Johnson's answer, perhaps fittingly, is more patience. "I just need him to stay with the process and continue to keep doing what he's doing," Johnson said. "There are times unfortunately when you're on a really good team and you're a younger player fighting to get into the rotation, you can do everything right. It doesn't mean you're going to get what you want." Patience wasn't always Reed's strong suit. item.title: Cowboys’ Jerry Jones Called Out for ‘Humiliating’ Decision
item.description: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones Getty There’s no question that the press conference held by Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker on Thursday of this week was decidedly uncomfortable. He conceded he was disappointed in the fact that his play-calling duties had been stripped, and that he was still the coordinator but in name only. The team moved all of the play-calling to veteran coach Mike Pettine, which makes Parker the coordinator with little to coordinate. It’s a situation in which it is easy to be sympathetic to Parker. At the same time, Parker was a disaster running the defense which, to be fair, has been battered by injury and did not get enough real investment from the team throughout the offseason. Still, Parker is the coordinator and the fact that this group can’t seem to cover receivers or tackle or defend the run ultimately falls on him. Cowboys Don’t Want to Pay Christian Parker After Firing Him? So you can’t hold it against the Cowboys for making a change but you can hold it against them for taking half measures. Keeping Parker on staff while leaving him enfeebled is awkward at best or, as veteran NFL insider Mike Florio said, “humiliating” at worst. And in the end, what it probably comes down to team owner Jerry Jones being penurious with his staff. The Cowboys took away defensive coordinator Christian Parker's play-calling duties but didn't fire him. Probably because Jerry Jones doesn't want to pay the buyout. pic.twitter.com/pI4BO38gTD — PFT Live (@PFT_Live) November 20, 2026 Said Florio during his “PFT” podcast : “ It is impossible not to look at this and suspect that Jerry Jones is hoping he will quit so he doesn’t have to buy him out. I think the best interests of the football team are served by firing Christian Parker and avoiding any confusion in the locker room, who’s really in charge, I am loyal to Christian Parker, well I’m loyal to Mike Pettine—you don’t need that. You just move on, like you would for a coach. “ This fits with the reputation that he does not like to pay coaches to not work. Go ahead and fire him, it is better for your team. He doesn’t want to be there at this point, it is humiliating. “ Parker will be on the sideline, with Pettine, as the Cowboys face the Titans on Sunday in Arlington at 1 p.m. ET. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. item.title: How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊
item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
